description:
From the fz-kdt.106 cold review (2026-09-01), corrected by the build.
On a 34-line program (14 element families x 14 distinct lambdas through
Enum.all?/2, parked at the review scratchpad as kdt106-review-stress1.fz)
the WORK numbers reproduce across two independent measurements: base 526
executables with 18-24 budget collapses -> 588 executables with 3
collapses under dominance absorption, same stdout, both schedules
confluent. The review's 172.8s -> 1.63s wall-clock headline did NOT
reproduce on the build round (0.80s base / 0.88s head, same machine
class) -- treat the wall-clock claim as unreproduced and build the
ratchet on WORK numbers only (settlement counts from --log-telemetry,
per fz-f98.23's no-wall-clock-on-CI law), which is what this ticket
requires anyway.

TWO DELIVERABLES:
(1) The standing CLASSIFICATION-GATE rationale (recorded here, referenced
by fz-kdt.106's close): "executable counts must not rise" is not a
property of dominance absorption -- the stress shape RISES 526->588
because precision replaces collapse-widened sharing. The correct gate:
a rise is acceptable exactly when paired with a reduction in budget
collapses on that fixture; anything else is a STOP.
(2) A corpus fixture in the collapse-cascade shape with a work-based
ratchet pinned against the fz-kdt.106-landed baseline. Note the landed
head still collapses 3x on the stress shape -- genuine correlation
width, by design; the fixture pins THAT number, not zero.
Blocked by fz-kdt.106 (needs its baseline + its telemetry event fz-0xp).
title: Budget-collapse cascades are a compile-work catastrophe the corpus never captures: add a collapse-cascade fixture with a work ratchet
